history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate - the temple is at Devarayanadurga, a hill station in Tumakuru district about 17-20 km from Tumkur city (65 km from Bengaluru). Documented with the corrected location. This is the famous hilltop Yoganarasimha temple of the Devarayanadurga group, at ~3940 ft among rocky hills and forests. Legend: Lord Brahma performed penance for thousands of years to please Vishnu, who manifested as Yoga Narasimha; the hill is also called Karigiri (Kari = elephant/black, Giri = hill - from its elephant-shaped silhouette, and the legend of the cursed Gandharva brothers Devadatta and Dhanunjaya turned into mountain and elephant) and Kusumadri (gods showered flowers/Pushpa on Vishnu after he slew the demon Pundarika). A Kalyani (sacred pond) and Shri Padha Theertha stand on the hilltop premises; a shrine of Lakshmi Devi stands next to the Lord. At the foot of the hill stands the Bhoga Narasimha temple (Dravidian style, east-facing, attributed to Kanthirava Narasaraja I, repaired 1858 by Krishnaraja Wodeyar III; tradition says sage Durvasa installed the idol; the deity is the family deity of the Mysore kings). NOTE: smaller shrines named Sri Yoganarasimha Swamy also exist at Dananayakanapura (~12 km from Tumkur) and Anupanahalli; if the CSV intended one of those, flag for correction.

name: Sri Yoganarasimha Swamy Temple
town: Devarayanadurga (CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate - the temple hill is ~17-20 km from Tumkur city, in Tumakuru district)
town_description: Devarayanadurga is a hill station in Tumakuru district at ~3940 ft, about 65 km from Bengaluru and 17-20 km from Tumkur, covered by rocky hills. The Yoganarasimha temple sits at the hilltop; the Bhoga Narasimha temple is at the hill base. Nearby: Namada Chilume (deer park) and a Forest Department medicinal-herb nursery; two springs Ane Done and Jaya Tirtha meet at the foot of Irukasandra hill.

travel.road: Drive from Bengaluru via Dabbaspet (~65 km); drive partway up and climb the last steps, or climb the stairs from the base; beware of monkeys.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Narasimha Jayanthi (May) is grand but hot and crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daytime darshan (typical hilltop temple hours 6:00 AM-8:00 PM - verify; not published).
